title: Did you know… Jesus spoke in parables that not everyone understood?
paragraphs: Did you know… Jesus spoke in parables that not everyone understood?

They heard the same words…
but walked away with completely different hearts.
Jesus didn’t hide truth.

He revealed it—
but only to those who were ready to surrender.
In Matthew 13, when Jesus Christ told the Parable of the Sower, the crowd leaned in.

Stories about seeds.
Soil.
Farming.
Simple, right?
But then He said something that shook everything:
“Whoever has ears, let them hear.”

Wait—
they all had ears.
So what did He mean?
The disciples asked Him privately, and Jesus answered with weight:

Some hear… but never understand.
Some see… but never perceive.
Why?

Because truth isn’t just heard.
It’s received.
And here’s the tension—don’t miss this:

Parables didn’t just reveal truth.
They exposed hearts.

Hard hearts hear stories and stay unchanged.
Hungry hearts hear God and fall to their knees.

Same message.
Different soil.
But here’s what we miss…
Jesus wasn’t trying to confuse people.
He was separating curiosity from surrender.

Because the Kingdom of God isn’t unlocked by intelligence—
it’s opened by repentance.
That’s the Gospel.

We were the hardened ground.
Closed. Resistant. Wandering.
But Jesus didn’t leave us there.

Through the cross, He broke the soil.
Through His blood, He planted grace.
Through His resurrection, He offers new life.

Now the question isn’t:
“Do you understand the story?”
It’s this:
Will you let the Word change you?
Today, don’t just listen.
Receive.

Repent.
Believe.
Follow Him.
And watch your life bear fruit you could never grow on your own.

From hidden truth to revealed grace—
because Jesus still speaks to those who are listening.
